decisions.executionNote: Raise both elbows into a continuous approach configuration, grippers open; then align to the two lower supports from RGB.
Align each open gripper with its rear white support, accounting for the angled blocks; approach conservatively above grasp height.
Lower to support grasp height, refine lateral alignment from wrist images, and close both grippers. Retention will be checked by lifting.
Lift both supports clear, straighten their yaw, and begin translating toward symmetric lower-layer positions with grippers closed.
Both supports remain visible in the grippers. Bring them to evenly spaced lower-layer locations, remaining above the table before the final descent.
Set the two upright supports down at matched height and release without lateral motion; next inspect their spacing and stability.
Withdraw vertically from the released supports, then move outward and start turning both grippers toward the ends of the long board.
The lower supports appear upright and separated evenly. Finish turning the open grippers inward above the long board before descending to its ends.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller wrist turns, then begin a shallow inward descent toward the long board's ends.
Approach the long board symmetrically at both ends and close the grippers. Keep the board level for a two-arm lift.
Lift the long board evenly clear of the table, then begin moving it toward the two upright supports while maintaining closed grippers.
Center the lifted long board over both supports, lower gently onto them, and open both grippers to release the lower layer.
The long board appears stable across its supports. Clear its ends and begin turning toward the remaining white blocks for the middle layer.
Finish aligning the grippers to the angled remaining blocks while moving above their grasp points, keeping clear of the completed lower layer.
Lower around the two remaining blocks, refine the right-hand yaw from its wrist view, and close both grippers for a retention check.
Lift the grasped blocks above the lower board, straighten their yaw, and start moving them inward while keeping both grippers closed.
Both blocks remain retained. Center them at symmetric middle-support positions and descend cautiously toward the lower board before release.
Seat the middle supports gently, open both grippers, and lift clear to inspect the upright pieces before fetching the middle board.
The released middle supports appear upright. Move away from the tower toward the middle board, gradually turning both open grippers inward.
Finish the symmetric board-grasp orientation with small wrist increments while approaching above the middle board's ends.
Lower around the middle board's ends and close both grippers symmetrically, ready for a level retention-check lift.
Lift the middle board level above the tower supports and begin bringing it toward the centered placement, maintaining both closed grippers.
Correct the small right-hand height and tilt mismatch, then center the retained middle board above its two supports before lowering.
Lower the centered middle board evenly onto the upright supports and release both grippers, leaving all lower pieces undisturbed.
Clear the completed middle layer with open grippers, then approach the green cap on the left and the small wooden top board on the right.
Approach above the two top pieces within their respective workspaces, pitching the left gripper for the cap and turning the right gripper to the small board's long axis.
Align and close around the green cap with the left arm. Finish the right-hand turn and refine its approach above the small top board before grasping.
Lift the green cap to verify retention and hold it clear on the left; refine the small board alignment and close the right gripper.
Lift the small board clear to verify the right grasp. Hold the retained cap high on the left, squared to the tower, while preparing the board placement.
The small board is visibly retained. Rotate it across the tower while bringing it inward at clearance height; keep the cap parked on the left.
Finish squaring and centering the small top board above the middle layer, retaining clearance before the final gentle descent.
Refine the small board's centering, lower it gently onto the middle layer, and release the right gripper while the left retains the cap.
Withdraw the open right gripper from the small board and bring the retained cap toward the tower, keeping the arms separated and the cap level.
Center the green cap over the small board with a shallow descent. Move the empty right arm outward and gradually toward its origin configuration.
Seat and release the centered green cap, then lift the left gripper clear. Continue returning the open right arm toward origin.
The cap remains on the top board after release. Withdraw the left arm clear of the tower and return both open grippers toward their origin poses.
All eight pieces appear upright and centered. Continue a small-increment return of the left arm while settling the right arm at origin, both grippers open.
Finish returning the left arm to origin with a tapered approach. Keep both grippers open and leave the visibly stable tower untouched.
